summary.text: Elizabeth Embry is a Democratic member of the Maryland House of Delegates from District 43A who was elected in November 2022 and has served since January 11, 2023, and she is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
A former prosecutor and assistant attorney general, she serves on the Judiciary Committee, where she chairs the Estates and Trusts Subcommittee.

paragraphs.text: Elizabeth Embry was born in Baltimore on March 2, 1977, and graduated from Baltimore City College in 1995, according to her General Assembly biography.
She earned a B.A. from Yale University in 1999 and a J.D. from Columbia University School of Law in 2004.

She was an assistant state's attorney in Baltimore City from 2004 to 2008, an assistant solicitor for the Baltimore City Law Department, interim director of the Mayor's Office for Criminal Justice, and deputy state's attorney from 2011 to 2015.

She then served as chief of the criminal division at the Maryland Office of the Attorney General from 2015 to 2018 and as a special assistant attorney general from 2019 to 2022, and she has been an adjunct professor at the University of Baltimore and University of Maryland law schools.
Embry has served on the Judiciary Committee since 2023 and in 2026 chairs its Estates and Trusts Subcommittee.
She is second vice chair of the Baltimore City House Delegation.
Ballotpedia reports that she advanced from the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary.
